previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and gout was admitted after a fall at home, presenting with rigors and elevated lactate. Initial concern for infection led to broad-spectrum antibiotics, but blood and urine cultures showed no growth, and symptoms were attributed to a gout flare and anterior tibialis tendinopathy. The patient experienced vomiting, resolved with a soft diet after identifying poor dentition as the cause. A planned steroid injection for tendonitis was aborted due to a partial tear identified on ultrasound. Colchicine was restarted, allopurinol increased, and a prednisone taper initiated for gout. The patient improved clinically, remained afebrile off antibiotics, and was discharged home on a revised medication regimen with outpatient follow-up for orthopedic evaluation.
problems: Partial tear of anterior tibialis tendon
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Shortness of breath.  Chest pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Single frontal radiograph of the chest was compared to multiple
prior examinations, most recent radiograph dated ___

FINDINGS:  Lung volumes are low.  A micronodular/interstitial pulmonary
abnormality is chronic.  Pericpheral pulmonary vessels are indistinct. In
light of chronic cardiomegaly and progressive hilar vascular englargement,
this is probably mild pulmonary edema. No focal abnormality is present to
suggest pneumonia. Minimal blunting of the left costophrenic angle is due to
trace pleural effusion.  No pneumothorax is present.  The aorta is generarlly
large and very tortuous but not focally dilated or changed.  Eventration of
the right hemidiaphragm is stable.  A central catheter has been removed.  A
remote left clavicle fracture is .  There are dense calcifications of the
abdominal aorta.

IMPRESSION:  Mild pulmonary edema.  Following treatment, conventional
radiographs should be obtained to evaluate chronic pulmonary micronodulation.
